about.title: Hermosa Beach Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Hermosa Beach is a small coastal city, but its residents still rely on nearby hospitals, urgent care clinics, and specialists throughout Los Angeles County for everything from routine surgeries to emergency treatment. When that care falls below an accepted standard, the effects can follow a person for years, whether it's a delayed diagnosis, a surgical error, or a medication mistake caught too late. California law recognizes that these cases are different from an ordinary injury claim: they involve strict notice requirements, tight filing windows, and mandatory expert review. A bad medical outcome by itself doesn't prove malpractice, which is why an honest evaluation of the facts matters. We handle medical malpractice claims for Hermosa Beach residents at no upfront fee; we review your medical records, explain what happened, and outline realistic next steps under California's specific malpractice rules.

whyChoose.title: Why Understanding MICRA Matters in Hermosa Beach

items.title: Strict, Short Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the injury and no more than three years from the date it occurred to file, and a required 90-day pre-suit notice must go out before that clock runs down. Missing these windows can end a valid claim before it starts.

items.title: A Rising Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: MICRA sets a statutory cap on non-economic damages, but that cap increases each year rather than staying fixed. We can explain how the current cap applies to your specific situation.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California cases nearly always need a qualified medical expert to establish that the care fell below an accepted standard. A bad outcome alone isn't enough, so this step is central to building a credible claim.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near Pier Avenue. Does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that an unfavorable result by itself doesn't establish malpractice; there has to be evidence that the care provided fell below an accepted medical standard. We can review your records and help you understand whether that standard was met.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Hermosa Beach?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, and no more than three years from the date it happened. Before filing suit, a 90-day pre-suit notice is also typically required. Because these deadlines are strict, it's worth speaking with us as soon as possible.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California's MICRA law places a cap specifically on non-economic damages, though that cap rises each year rather than staying the same. Economic losses, like medical bills and lost income, are handled separately. We can walk you through how these categories apply to your situation.
